title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.
intro: This training programme equips investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations that identify criminal proceeds, trace money through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence that stands up in court.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give investigators and analysts the methods to make financial investigation a routine part of every case involving profit-generating crime. Participants leave able to obtain and analyse financial records, unpick corporate structures, calculate criminal benefit and present clear, defensible findings to prosecutors and the court.
sections.What It Covers: The purpose and principles of financial investigation, planning parallel investigations, sources of financial information, production orders and other powers, analysing bank and payment records, cash and informal value transfer, net-worth and source-and-application-of-funds analysis, corporate vehicles and beneficial ownership, digital and crypto-asset evidence, and presenting financial findings.
Intended Audience: Police and agency investigators handling acquisitive, organised or economic crime
Financial investigators, intelligence analysts and FIU staff supporting investigations
Asset recovery, customs and tax investigators who trace and evidence criminal finances
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose of parallel financial investigation and when to start one
Identify and obtain financial information lawfully using the appropriate powers
Analyse bank, payment and cash records to establish money flows and patterns
Apply net-worth and source-and-application-of-funds methods to evidence criminal benefit
Trace funds through companies, trusts and nominees to their beneficial owners
Present financial findings clearly to prosecutors, courts and partner agencies
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with worked records and case exercises, ending in an investigation workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the participants' roles and caseload.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of criminal investigation, intelligence analysis or financial crime work is helpful. No accounting qualification is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012), Operational Issues: Financial Investigations Guidance
FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
FATF and Egmont Group (2018), Concealment of Beneficial Ownership
FATF (2023), Guidance on Beneficial Ownership for Legal Persons

modules.title: Financial Investigation: Purpose and Principles
modules.summary: Why every profit-generating crime should have a financial dimension, the objectives a financial investigation can serve, and what the FATF standards expect of investigative authorities.
objectives: Explain the evidential, intelligence and asset recovery purposes of financial investigation
Distinguish parallel financial investigations from stand-alone money laundering cases
Summarise the FATF expectations for investigative powers and outcomes
syllabus: Following the money: proving offences, finding assets and mapping networks
Parallel financial investigation alongside predicate offence cases
FATF Recommendations 30 and 31 and Immediate Outcome 7
The financial investigator's role in a multi-disciplinary team

modules.title: Planning and Managing a Financial Investigation
modules.summary: How to scope a financial investigation, set objectives and hypotheses, prioritise lines of enquiry and manage records, exhibits and disclosure from the outset.
objectives: Set investigation objectives, hypotheses and a lines-of-enquiry plan
Prioritise enquiries in proportion to risk and resources
Maintain decision logs, exhibits and audit trails from the start
syllabus: Scoping: subjects, periods, predicate offences and assets
Investigation plans, hypotheses and lines of enquiry
Coordination with intelligence, asset recovery and prosecutors
Record-keeping, decision logs and early disclosure planning

modules.title: Sources of Financial Information
modules.summary: The open, closed and restricted sources investigators can use to build a financial profile, and how to assess their reliability and the conditions attached to their use.
objectives: Identify open, closed and restricted sources of financial information
Assess reliability, completeness and handling conditions
Build an initial financial profile of a subject
syllabus: Public registers: companies, land, vehicles and court records
FIU intelligence and tax, customs and law-enforcement holdings
Open-source research and lifestyle indicators
Building the subject's financial profile

modules.title: Investigative Powers: Production Orders and Beyond
modules.summary: The legal tools for obtaining financial records and information, how to draft applications that are precise and justified, and how to work effectively with the institutions that must comply.
objectives: Explain the main powers to obtain financial information and their thresholds
Draft focused, justified applications for production and disclosure orders
Manage institution responses, deadlines and data formats
syllabus: Production, disclosure, account monitoring and customer information orders
Search, seizure and powers to obtain electronic records
Drafting applications: necessity, proportionality and specificity
Working with institutions: contacts, formats and confidentiality

modules.title: Analysing Bank and Payment Records
modules.summary: Techniques for reading and analysing account statements, payment data and supporting documents to identify patterns, links and anomalies that test the investigation's hypotheses.
objectives: Read account opening, statement and payment records accurately
Apply spreadsheet and analytical techniques to large transaction sets
Identify patterns indicating laundering, fraud or hidden assets
syllabus: Account opening files, statements, payment messages and card data
Cleaning, normalising and reconciling transaction data
Pattern analysis: round sums, pass-through activity and structuring
Charting money flows and counterparties

modules.title: Cash, Value Transfer and Alternative Remittance
modules.summary: How criminal cash is moved, stored and converted, how informal value transfer and alternative remittance operate, and the evidence investigators can obtain about them.
objectives: Explain how cash proceeds are placed and moved
Describe informal value transfer and alternative remittance systems
Identify evidence sources for cash-based and informal transfers
syllabus: Cash-intensive businesses and cash deposits
Cross-border cash movements and declarations
Informal value transfer and alternative remittance
Evidencing cash: seizures, ledgers and communications

modules.title: Net-Worth and Source-and-Application-of-Funds Analysis
modules.summary: Indirect methods for proving unexplained income and wealth, how to build a defensible net-worth or source-and-application-of-funds analysis, and how these support charges and confiscation.
objectives: Explain when indirect methods of proof are appropriate
Build a net-worth and a source-and-application-of-funds statement
Test the analysis against likely defence explanations
syllabus: Direct versus indirect methods of proof
Net-worth method: assets, liabilities, expenditure and known income
Source-and-application-of-funds statements
Anticipating defences: cash savings, gifts, loans and inheritances

modules.title: Corporate Vehicles and Beneficial Ownership
modules.summary: How companies, trusts, foundations and nominees are used to conceal ownership and move funds, and how investigators trace control through registers, records and cooperation.
objectives: Recognise how legal persons and arrangements are misused to conceal ownership
Trace control and beneficial ownership using registers and institution records
Identify the role of professional enablers
syllabus: Shell, shelf and front companies, trusts and nominee arrangements
Beneficial ownership registers, service provider records and their limits
Mapping ownership and control across jurisdictions
Professional enablers: lawyers, accountants and company service providers

modules.title: Digital Payments and Crypto-Asset Evidence
modules.summary: Obtaining and interpreting evidence from payment firms, e-money issuers, online platforms and crypto-asset service providers, and integrating it with traditional financial records.
objectives: Identify the records held by payment, e-money and crypto-asset service providers
Integrate digital payment and blockchain data into the financial picture
Recognise the evidential limits of analytics outputs
syllabus: Payment firms, e-money accounts and online marketplaces
Crypto-asset service provider records and blockchain tracing basics
Device, communications and other digital financial evidence
Attribution, reliability and continuity of digital evidence

modules.title: Presenting Financial Findings: Investigation Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams analyse records, trace funds through corporate vehicles, calculate benefit and present their findings to a mock prosecution review.
objectives: Prepare clear financial statements, charts and summaries for prosecutors and courts
Explain analysis and assumptions under challenge
Apply the programme's methods to a realistic case
syllabus: Writing financial investigation reports and witness statements
Charts, schedules and summaries that courts can follow
Giving evidence and handling cross-examination on financial analysis
Workshop: tracing, benefit calculation and case presentation

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.

related.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
